texts.facts: On the basis of the said fardbayan, Dehri Town P.S. Case no. 163 of 2013, dated March 24, 2013, came to be registered under Section 285, 286, 308, and 120 B IPC against the proprietor and staff of R.D. Indonesian Gas Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4) dt.01-04-2024 Agency. When the gas was leaking, no one put a safety cap on it to stop the leakage. As the leakage increased, LPG was sprayed over a wide Ruchi Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 1 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157360348/ 2 area, and a backfire towards the cylinder took place. From the physical examination of the cylinder at police custody, it was evident that the valve and o- ring were not damaged, and the pin was stuck at that time. Therefore, after engaging the regulator with the cylinder, the foreign particle may have stuck. The LPG accident occurred on March 24, 2013. Taking into consideration the reports as well as other facts that came into light during the investigation, the Sub Divisional Police officer directed the investigating officer to submit the final report on the ground of "lack of evidence." However, the Superintendent of Police, Rohtas, did not agree with the supervision report of the sub-divisional police officer and directed the I.O. to submit a charge sheet against Ruchi Singh, ( the proprietor ), Ambika Singh, ( Supervisor ), Lalan Paswan, ( storekeeper ), and Md. Ibrahim, ( technician), whereupon Charge-sheet No. 520/2016, dated December 31, 2016, was filed against these persons under secs. 285, 304, 308, and 34 IPC. The case was committed to the Court of the 3rd Additional District Judge by order dated August 18, 2022. In case of leakage, the safety cap supplied with the cylinder should have been immediately fixed, which was not done by Santosh Kumar. He has nothing to do with the workings of the gas agency. Lalan Paswan is the storekeeper of the gas agency, whose duty it is only to store the gas cylinders.
texts.arguments: 6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the opposite party opposed the arguments advanced on behalf of the petitioners and submitted that due to the leakage of the cylinder, Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.43838 of 2023(4) dt.01-04-2024 some persons became injured due to the spread of fire; eighteen persons sustained injuries, out of which ten died. It is also apparent from the record that, after the completion of the investigation, a charge sheet has been submitted against the owner, operator, storekeeper, etc. of the offending gas agency.

annotations_dropped.text_preview: As such, no offence is made out against these petitioners, and the present application is fit to be quashed.
He next submits that there are sufficient materials on record against these petitioners, and it cannot be said that prima facie no case is made against these petitioners.
Hence, no interference is required by this court at this stage .

7. From bare perusal of the FIR, it is apparent that the informant was not aware whether the cylinder in question was supplied by the agency or not, and he came to know about this fact only through his neighbor Santosh Kumar.
During the course of the investigation, it has also come in light that the cylinder in question was not delivered by the aforementioned agency or its staff.
Continuation of proceedings against these petitioners would amount to abuse of the process of the court.
